findings.statement: CXCR2 is a neutrophil gene: neutrophils make most of its inflamed-mucosa transcripts [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]. Smillie (no neutrophils) assigns it to T/NK and the second dataset to myeloid, so the lineage attribution is not replicated there and is a capture artefact. After composition adjustment the change shrinks but stays significant (partly_composition) [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409].

CXCL8 bulk increase is essentially cell influx: neutrophils carry most transcripts in Gubatan [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873] (myeloid dominant in Smillie, macrophages first, replicated in the second dataset). The adjusted change is no longer significant (verdict composition) [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0523]. It is a marker of myeloid/neutrophil influx rather than a tissue-intrinsic change; adjustment may over-correct activated resident cells.

IDO1 is made mainly by myeloid cells (macrophages, DC1; Smillie and the second dataset agree) with minimal neutrophil contribution [gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.072]. Change remains significant after adjustment (partly_composition) [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505], supporting a real tissue change in myeloid cells.

MMP1 comes from inflammatory fibroblasts (stromal lineage, replicated in the second dataset); in Visium deconvolution inflammatory fibroblasts explain most of the in-situ signal [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.579]. The change survives adjustment (partly_composition) [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]. CosMx detection was not above background, so single-cell spatial confirmation is lacking.

DUOX2 is epithelial (enterocytes) [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947], replicated in the second dataset and in Xenium and Visium, with the epithelial group the top in-situ source. It keeps a strong adjusted change [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161], so it is an epithelial-intrinsic induction, the cleanest tissue-change candidate.

CHI3L1 is stromal, from inflammatory fibroblasts, replicated in the second dataset [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.941], though neutrophils also contribute a sizeable share in Gubatan. It retains a significant adjusted change [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967].

S100A8 is predominantly neutrophil-derived [gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909], so it is a marker of neutrophil influx; some change persists after adjustment (partly_composition) [gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.9231].

LCN2 loses its bulk change after adjustment (verdict composition) [gene=LCN2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.206], even though neutrophils are not its main source in Gubatan, so the increase tracks overall cellular composition shifts (possibly epithelial loss); over-correction is possible.

AQP9 is overwhelmingly neutrophil-derived [gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92] and its adjusted change is smaller but still significant (partly_composition) [gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8551]. It is mainly a neutrophil-influx marker.

CD274 (PD-L1) has a mixed source: neutrophils contribute a large share in Gubatan [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687], while Smillie assigns plasma cells, macrophages and enterocytes with myeloid dominance replicated. Adjusted change persists (partly_composition) [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978].

caveats: Smillie 2019 did not capture neutrophils, so lineage attribution of neutrophil genes (CXCR2, CXCR1, CXCL8) from that dataset is unreliable; Gubatan neutrophil shares are used instead.
Composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells become activated; loss of significance (CXCL8, LCN2) is not proof of pure influx, and retained change is only partial for most genes.
Shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance. CXCR1, CXCL1, MMP10 and other ranked genes were assessed only through the batch neutrophil-share query, not individually.
MMP1 is not above background on CosMx and not on Xenium; Visium spot co-variation is weaker evidence than single-cell data.
